transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan, Marco Li (Redwood); Linda Park, Owen Byers, Nadia Cross (Argent Systems)

Summary: quick poc scoping focused on latency SLO definition — TTFT vs TPOT, p95/p99 targets, measurement plan, and timeline for a 4-week pilot. Agreed actions: Argent to share workload traces; Redwood to run pilot benchmarks (hosted + dedicated) and present results; follow-up next week.

Topics:
- Success criteria (business metrics, acceptable latency windows)
- Workload sizing (qps, seq len distributions)
- Benchmarks (TTFT vs TPOT definitions, measurement tooling)
- Targets (p95/p99, warm vs cold start)
- Measurement plan and dashboards
- Timeline and gating for POC -> pilot -> prod

Transcript: (note: auto-transcript, some words may be off)
00:00 Speaker 1 (Samira): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to focus this time on the latency SLOs for the POC and how we'll measure them. Linda and team, thanks for sharing your initial goals in the form.
00:27 Linda Park: yeah hi thanks, yep basically we need to be confident that the model responses are under a user-acceptable latency for our main flows. Our main concern is low-latency chat and a search rerank pipeline that feeds UI. We're trying to define whether we should optimize for TTFT or TPOT.
00:45 Marco Li: quick clarifier — by TTFT you mean time-to-first-token, which captures that first visible char in the UI, and TPOT is time-to-probable-termination or time-to-last-token, basically full response latency, right?
01:10 Linda Park: yeah TTFT is important for perceived snappiness on chat, TPOT matters for the batch reranker where we need full output. We have two classes of traffic: interactive chat (peak 120 qps, median seq len ~80 tokens) and batch re-rank (peak 20 qps, seq len ~300).
01:36 Marco Li: got it, that's helpful. Owen, can you confirm that 120 qps is concurrent requests or total qps?
01:44 Owen Byers: that's concurrent user-facing QPS at peak across our US region, about 95% are short chats under 150 tokens, but we do have tails to 1k tokens in some debug flows.
02:00 Nadia Cross: and our success criteria is basically keeping perceived chat latency under 200ms TTFT p95, and rerank full response TPOT p95 under 700ms. Those numbers are target-ish, we'll listen to Redwood's take on feasibility.
02:19 Samira Khan: ok that's a good starting point. From Redwood's experience - for hosted models on an A100 class GPU with batching and prefix caching, TTFT p95 ~ 150-250ms is achievable for short sequences if you tune batching carefully. For TPOT p95 it's more dependent on model size and kv cache behavior.
02:42 Marco Li: and we should be clear about warm vs cold. Warm requests (i.e., with KV cache hit and active session) will be much faster — cold starts, container spinup or cold weights may add 200-500ms for some deployment modes. For Redwood Dedicated we can provision warm pools to reduce cold starts.
03:10 Linda Park: that's actually critical — our product team says cold starts over 1s are unacceptable. So we need an explicit gating rule in the POC to show <1s cold start 95th or fallback.
03:23 Samira Khan: noted. Let's talk about measurement: we'll run two benchmark types — synthetic replay of your traces (replay with timing preserved) and a synthetic QPS driver that does open-loop load tests for TPOT p95/p99. We'll measure TTFT by instrumenting at the request edge and also capture per-token generation time if possible.
03:48 Marco Li: we typically instrument with three markers: request arrival, first token emitted, final token emitted. From those we compute TTFT = time(firstToken - arrival) and TPOT = time(lastToken - arrival). We'll also measure model-side breakdowns: attention/forward time, kv cache retrieval, network overhead.
04:10 Owen Byers: can you show example dashboards or the schema of the benchmark spreadsheet?
04:16 Marco Li: sure I'll share our benchmark spreadsheet link after the call - it's a template with columns: timestamp, seq_len, prompt_type, qps_profile, request_latency_ms, first_token_ms, last_token_ms, memory_usage, gpu_util. (we'll post link: https://drive.google.com/benchmark-argent )
04:40 Linda Park: perfect. For SLOs we want p95 and p99 for both TTFT and TPOT. Example targets we mentioned: chat TTFT p95 <200ms, p99 <400ms; rerank TPOT p95 <700ms, p99 <1.2s. Are those realistic?
05:00 Marco Li: they are aggressive but within scope depending on model size and whether you go dedicated or hosted. If you want obligations, Redwood Dedicated with pinned capacity and optimized kernels gives better tail than elastic hosted. Also quantization can impact TPOT by reducing compute time but may change quality.
05:24 Nadia Cross: quality tradeoff is a big part of our acceptance criteria — we need to ensure quantized runs don't drop accuracy beyond a 2% BLEU-like metric on our eval set. We'll include quality checks in the benchmark.
05:40 Samira Khan: good to include. For measurement windows, we recommend measuring under: steady-state warm conditions, cold-start scenarios, and during autoscale events. Each benchmark run should be at least 15 minutes for steady-state to capture tails, and shorter 5 min runs for cold-start experiments.
06:02 Owen Byers: what's your recommended load shaping? I assume ramp up and a few spikes to surface autoscaler behavior?
06:10 Marco Li: yes: a 10 min ramp to peak, 20 min steady at peak, two 1 min spikes at 2x peak, then 10 min ramp down. We'll also replay 48h of real traffic at production timing to capture realistic inter-arrival distributions for p99 tail.
06:29 Linda Park: ok timeline wise, can we get initial benchmark results in one week? We have a holiday freeze in two weeks so want to conclude pilot by mid-Jan.
06:38 Samira Khan: we can start bench runs as soon as you share traces; preliminary hosted results in 4 business days, dedicated run will take ~7 business days to provision and run. So that aligns with mid-Jan gate.
06:55 Nadia Cross: for the POC acceptance criteria, we want three things: 1) TTFT and TPOT meet p95 targets for respective flows, 2) p99 within 2x p95 (no pathological tails), 3) quality regression <2% on eval set. If any fail, we'll surface mitigation steps — batching tuning, model variant, or dedicated capacity.
07:20 Marco Li: good framing. Also we propose a measurement plan doc where we define exact metrics, instrumentation points, dashboards (Redwood Console links), and a golden prompt set for quality checks. We'll share that doc.
07:34 Linda Park: can you also include cost estimates — tokens and per-hour GPU numbers — so we can compare dedicated vs hosted?
07:41 Samira Khan: yes we'll include estimated cost per 1k requests and per-hour for dedicated capacity. For initial bench we'll provide a rough delta: hosted tends to be higher per token for tail heavy workload but lower ops overhead. Dedicated is cheaper at scale but requires commit.
07:58 Owen Byers: a technical question — how do you handle KV cache across sessions? Our product uses long context across sessions, and we worry about stale cache or cross-tenant leakage.
08:10 Marco Li: Redwood uses per-session KV namespaces, and we can bring-your-own-KMS for Private deployments. For Dedicated we can configure isolated pools per customer. In transcript the auto-transcriber sometimes shows K/V cash or K V cache as K V cash - but the idea is per-session kv caching.
08:33 Linda Park: ok security team will want SOC2 docs and an architecture diagram for VPC peering — can you share that?
08:40 Samira Khan: yes we'll send SOC2 summary and the VPC peering diagram; we'll also add notes about audit logs and SSO.
08:48 Nadia Cross: back to measurement, do you instrument client-side or server-side for TTFT? We want to compare client perceived TTFT vs server emission.
08:56 Marco Li: both. Server-side markers capture times at the model runtime; client-side captures network and render overhead. We'll correlate them. For the spreadsheet we'll add columns for client_observed_first_ms and server_emitted_first_ms.
09:15 Linda Park: for the p99 measurement we want 95th, 99th, and 99.9th, but I understand 99.9 is noisy. Maybe report 99.9 with confidence intervals.
09:25 Samira Khan: agreed. We'll provide confidence intervals and bootstrapped p99.9 to avoid overinterpreting outliers.
09:35 Marco Li: quick note on sampling rates — for very high qps measuring every request at the server may be heavy; we recommend full capture for a sample window and statistical sampling elsewhere. We'll document sampling strategy.
09:55 Owen Byers: on the tooling side, can we get the benchmark harness open-sourced or a runbook? Our infra team wants to reproduce tests.
10:03 Marco Li: yes the harness is a private repo but we can share a sanitized runbook and a reproducible harness config. For enterprise customers we can provide the harness or container images.
10:20 Linda Park: any thoughts about model variants? We may test an LLM-7B and a trimmed 3B variant. We care about TPOT for the 7B but TTFT for 3B.
10:30 Marco Li: that's a sensible matrix. We'll include 3 model variants: 3B quantized, 7B fp16, and a tuned 7B int8-ish variant. We'll measure quality vs latency and provide recommendation.
10:46 Nadia Cross: we want to see per-route cost estimates since rerank is very different than chat.
10:53 Samira Khan: yes per-route dashboards in Redwood Console will show token counts, latency, and cost. We'll share screenshots in the follow-up.
11:05 Linda Park: one more constraint — our legal team requires data residency in US only for this pilot. We'll note that.
11:12 Samira Khan: we can ensure region pinning to US regions for the pilot; for Private deployments we can support on-prem later.
11:20 Owen Byers: anything else on instrumentation? We want to tag requests with correlation IDs and include model-version and host id in traces.
11:28 Marco Li: yes include metadata: model_version, host_id, batch_id, kv_hit boolean. That'll allow tail analysis.
11:36 Samira Khan: let's recap next steps: Argent sends traces and sample prompts by 2026-12-23; Redwood runs hosted bench and shares spreadsheet by 2026-12-24; Redwood spins up dedicated run and shares by 2026-12-30; follow-up meeting week of 2026-12-27 to review hosted results and set final acceptance gates.
11:58 Linda Park: sounds good. We'll also prepare the quality eval set and share SOC2 request doc.
12:08 Samira Khan: great. Action items captured in the sheet and I'll follow up with calendar invites. Thanks everyone.
12:18 (call ends, small crosstalk)

Notes: transcript contains occasional mishears, e.g., "TTFT" was sometimes transcribed as "T-T-F-T" and KV cache as "K V cash"; timestamps approximate. Reference artifacts: benchmark template (drive link above), Redwood Console demo screenshot (will be shared), SOC2 summary (link forthcoming).

POC acceptance checklist (agreed):
- TTFT p95 and p99 targets for chat: p95 <200ms, p99 <400ms (warm)
- TPOT p95 and p99 targets for rerank: p95 <700ms, p99 <1200ms
- Cold start p95 <1s
- Quality regression <2% vs baseline on eval set
- Per-route cost estimates and a runbook for reproducibility

Measurement plan (high-level):
- Instrumentation: arrival_ts, first_token_ts, last_token_ts, client_first_render, model_version, host_id, kv_hit
- Benchmark types: replay (real traces with preserved timing), open-loop QPS driver, cold-start experiments
- Reporting windows: steady-state (15+ min), stress spikes, cold-start tests (repeat N=10), 48h replay for tails
- Metrics to report: TTFT p50/p95/p99/p999, TPOT p50/p95/p99/p999, throughput (qps), GPU util, memory, cost per 1k requests
